Maps each known region (see {@link CityRegionTable}) to the inclusive range of 26 * 4-digit postcodes valid within it: NSW 2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099. 27 * A region with no known range accepts any postcode. This is the single source of 28 * truth for the mapping, so callers never repeat the table. 29 */ 30 public final class RegionPostcodeTable { 31 32 private static final Map RANGE_BY_REGION = Map.of( 33 "NSW", new int[] {2000, 2099}, 34 "VIC", new int[] {3000, 3099}, 35 "QLD", new int[] {4000, 4099}); 36 37 private RegionPostcodeTable() { 38 } 39 40 /** 41 * Resolve the canonical region whose postcode range contains the given postcode. 42 * 43 * @param postcode a postcode value, which may be {@code null} or non-numeric 44 * @return the region owning the range that contains the postcode, or an empty 45 * {@link Optional} when the postcode is absent, unparseable or in no known range 46 */ 47 public static Optional regionFor(String postcode) { 48 if (postcode == null || !postcode.chars().allMatch(Character::isDigit) || postcode.isEmpty()) { 49 return Optional.empty(); 50 } 51 int value = Integer.parseInt(postcode); 52 return RANGE_BY_REGION.entrySet().stream() 53 .filter(e -> value >= e.getValue()[0] && value <= e.getValue()[1]) 54 .map(Map.Entry::getKey) 55 .findFirst(); 56 } 57 58 /** 59 * Whether the given postcode falls within the range valid for the region. 60 * 61 * @param region the canonical region (as returned by {@link CityRegionTable}) 62 * @param postcode the numeric postcode value 63 * @return {@code true} if the region has no known range (permissive default) or the 64 * postcode is within its inclusive range, {@code false} otherwise 65 */ 66 public static boolean accepts(String region, int postcode) { 67 int[] range = RANGE_BY_REGION.get(region); 68 return range == null || (postcode >= range[0] && postcode <= range[1]); 69 } 70 } 71
